project.title: Proteomics analysis of differentially expressed proteins in lung cancer H157 cells after overexpression of AACT with data‐independent acquisition mass spectrometry
project.projectDescription: H157 cells transfected with vector and overexpressed AACT plasmids were treated and used for MS detection. The MS data were acquired using an Orbitrap Exploris 480 Mass Spectrometer coupled with an EASY-NLC 1200 liquid phase LC-MS system. DIA raw data files were analyzed by DIA-NN software. The differentially expressed proteins were screened in this quantitative proteomics.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: H157 cells transfected with vector and overexpressed AACT plasmids were collected and quickly frozen with liquid nitrogen. The samples were further detected by SpecAlly Life Technology Co., LTD (Wuhan, China). The proteins were denatured, reduced and alkylated with reaction solution containing 1% sodium deoxycholate, 100 mM Tris-HCl with pH 8.5, 10 mM trichloroethyl phosphate, and 40 mM chloroacetamide by one-step at 60 ℃ for 1 h, and digested with trypsin overnight at 37 ℃. The digestion reaction was stopped by trifluoroacetic acid, and the digested peptides were desalted and evaporated.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: The MS data were acquired using an Orbitrap Exploris 480 Mass Spectrometer coupled with an EASY-NLC 1200 liquid phase LC-MS system. Peptide samples were aspirated by an autosampler and bound to a C18 analytical column for separation. The mobile phases A consisted of 0.1 % formic acid and mobile phases B consisted of 0.1% formic acid and 80% ACN acetonitrile (ACN) were used to establish the analytical gradient. The flow rate was maintained at 300 nL/min. The mass spectrometry data was collected with DIA model, and each cycle included one MS1 scan (Max IT was 30 ms, scan range from 350 to 1250 m/z) and 40 MS2 scans with variable windows (Max IT = 50 ms), and the collision energy was set to 30. DIA raw data files were analyzed by DIA-NN software (V 1.8). The human proteome reference database in Uniprot (2021-03-12, containing 20381 protein sequences) was used for search analysis. The spectrum libraries were obtained via the deep learning algorithm in DIA-NN and MBR function, and the spectrum libraries were used to extract the original DIA data to obtain protein quantitative information. The final results were screened by 1% FDR for parent ion and protein levels. The quantitative information of the proteome after screening was used for subsequent analysis.
